counterevidence_considered.observed_value: within-unit repeated measurements pre-aggregated to one value per week

evidence.description: The data description names segment_id as the independent-unit column and defines one trial as one row, so the unit-to-row mapping expected by the sign test is one row per independent unit.

evidence.description: data/input.csv contains exactly 24 data rows with segment_id values S01 through S24, each appearing exactly once and with all street names distinct; no independent unit contributes more than one row.
The workflow explicitly refuses any input file in which a segment_id repeats, so the row-independent sign test cannot receive multiple rows from the same independent unit.
evidence.observed_value: SystemExit raised on duplicate segment_id before the test runs

evidence.description: The reported trial count equals the number of unique independent units: the sign test is run on 24 trials, and I independently recomputed 18 negative and 6 positive changes from the raw CSV, matching the reported 18-of-24 split and p = 0.022656.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I actively tried to demonstrate the issue: I scanned all 24 CSV rows for repeated segment_id values (none; S01-S24 each occur once), checked street_name for repeats that might reveal one street entered under multiple segment IDs (all 24 names are distinct, and the description states no two segments share a carriageway, junction, or corridor), and looked for any auxiliary column that could group multiple rows under one underlying unit (the header has none). I traced the analysis code to confirm the tested trial count is len(changes) built from one change per row with no row duplication, resampling, or per-night expansion, and that a duplicate-ID input would abort before testing. I also recomputed the sign counts from the raw data (18 quieter, 6 louder of 24) and confirmed they match the reported result, so the reported n equals the number of distinct independent units. No route by which a single independent unit enters the sign test more than once could be constructed from the supplied files.
